### Read the Bible: 2 Chronicles 14–15, Revelation 4, Haggai 2, and John 3
Author: D. A. Carson
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/devotionals/read-the-bible/2-chronicles-14-15-revelation-4-haggai-2-john-3/
Passage: 2 Chronicles 14–15
Points:
- Asa begins his reign by removing idols and commanding Judah to seek God, leading to peace and prosperity.
- When attacked by an overwhelming Cushite army, Asa acknowledges utter helplessness and relies entirely on God's power for victory.
- Encouraged by the prophet Azariah, Asa deepens national reform and renews Judah's covenant loyalty to the Lord.
- The account demonstrates that God providentially blesses righteousness, which strengthens and exalts a faithful community.

### Bible Pathways 05/25/2002
Author: Bible Pathway Ministries
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/biblepathways/bible-pathways-05-or-25-or-2002-1133454.html
Passage: 2 Chronicles 14:2-4
Points:
- Asa took a firm stand for moral and spiritual integrity by removing foreign altars and calling Judah to obey God's law.
- Standing firmly for the Lord often invites intense spiritual opposition, illustrated by the invasion of Zerah's massive army.
- Outnumbered, Asa placed his dependence upon God through prayer rather than despairing or yielding to fear.
- Seeking the Lord brought Judah divine rest and deliverance, pointing forward to soul rest in Christ.
- Asa's life serves as a warning against letting growing wealth and self-reliance erode continual dependence on prayer.
